proves: The plain governed hit: one catalog row, one long form, source governed, and the catalog row named in entry_id. This is rule 3 of the resolution order with keep_as_abbrev off.
Rule 3 with keep_as_abbrev on reports APPROVED rather than GOVERNED. The token is itself the governed physical form, and expansion still returns the long form.
Lookup is case-insensitive, and raw keeps the token exactly as the schema spelled it so a caller can align the answer back onto its own row.

The headline case. The pin wins over the most frequent candidate (Identity, declared first) and over what the scorer would pick, and beat records the seven long forms it was chosen over, in the catalog's own order.
A domain pin overrides the catalog's own default. Department is declared first and is what a most-frequent rule reaches for; the pin says Deposit and the pin decides.
A class-word entry surfaces its class word on the expansion, so a caller learns what kind of value the column holds without a second lookup.
A proper-noun acronym is not expanded and is not re-cased. ZIP stays ZIP: it is neither Zone Improvement Plan nor the Title Cased Zip a passthrough would have produced.
A short English word is accepted as a word. Five upper-case letters look like an abbreviation to a naive rule; the catalog says otherwise and the kind records it.
A short full word carried by the allow list alone, with no catalog row: known, approved, its own expansion, and entry_id null because there is no row to cite.
An unapproved abbreviation still expands. Being known and being permitted in a physical name are separate questions; the confidence below 1.0 marks the row as unconfirmed.
Rule 4: an allow-list member with no catalog row is known and approved, and its expansion is the token itself. There is nothing to expand it to and nothing is invented.
TOTAL sits in both common_keywords and short_full_words. The consult order decides, and it decides for the earlier list, so the kind is not SHORT_FULL_WORD.

Rule 5: a collision nobody pinned falls to canonical_form_score, which charges the gerund 50 and the past participle 30 and takes the bare noun. The source says SCORED so a reviewer can tell a rule of thumb from a recorded decision.

Rule 6. The vocabulary has never heard of KYC, so it comes back Title Cased for legibility with is_known false and confidence 0.0 - the absence of an answer, not a low-confidence one. Nothing is guessed and nothing is stemmed towards a near match.
The expansion of nothing is nothing, reported rather than raised, so a blank cell in a schema export does not stop a batch. kind is null because no rule fired at all.
Whitespace-only input is the empty case, and raw still carries what was supplied.
